text.p: This is how major world bond markets were trading in late European business on Monday.

GERMANY - German Bunds held on to their gains in late trade, shrugging off better-than-expected regional inflation data as the market remained firmly rangebound ahead of Tuesday's Federal Open Market Committee (FOMC) meeting. The June Bund future on the London International Financial Futures and Options Exchange (LIFFE) was trading at 100.10, up 0/16 from Friday's settlement price.

BRITAIN - Gilts ended a little higher with volumes thin ahead of Tuesday's U.S. FOMC meeting, Wednesday's gilt auction and the approaching Easter break, traders said the market is unlikely to make much headway until the auction has been and gone. The June long gilt future on LIFFE was trading at 109-08/32, up 02/32 from Friday's settlement price.

FRANCE - French bond futures finished the MATIF trading session just inside positive territory on the eve of a Federal Reserve meeting where an increase in U.S. interest rates is being predicted by the bulk of market experts. The June notional bond future on the MATIF in Paris settled at 127.86, up 0.02 from Friday's settlement price.

ITALY - Italian debt markets were weak as technical supports caved in and market fell through, dealers said they saw no big reason to sell BTPs with lira not strong but at least holding relatively steady, mini-budget expected later this week but first market is waiting to see what FOMC does to U.S. rates at Tuesday's meeting. The June bond future on LIFFE was trading at 124.47, down 0.61 from Friday's settlement price.

UNITED STATES - US Treasuries were narrowly higher at midmorning with little movement seen before the FOMC meets on Tuesday, short end stable as coupons continue to outperform, with trading volume very light as tightening widely expected. The June Treasury bond future on the Chicago Board of Trade was trading at 108-28/32, up 05/32 from Friday's settlement price. The long bond was quoted to yield 6.95 percent.

JAPAN - Key June Japanese government bond (JGB) futures ended the Tokyo session down, but well off earlier lows as short-covering pressure intensified following an afternoon plunge in Tokyo stocks. In after hours trading the June future on LIFFE was trading at 125.05, down 0.40 from Friday's settlement price on the Tokyo Stock Exchange.

EUROBONDS - Primary market activity was minimal with most of the market sidelined ahead of Tuesday's Federal Open Market Committee (FOMC). In the sterling market NatWest Markets launched a well-flagged 972 million stering securitised bond backed by Housing Association loans. The deal was split into seven tranches, with the largest a 728 million stering issue. With an average life of 28.6 years, these bonds will be priced the yield 60 b.p. over gilts.
